name: Familial Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Renal Papillary Neoplasia
aliases: Hereditary Papillary Thyroid and Renal Carcinoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Familial Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Renal Papillary Neoplasia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of at least two first-degree relatives with papillary thyroid carcinoma and/or renal papillary neoplasia
Histologically confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma in affected individuals
Histologically confirmed renal papillary neoplasia (type 1 or 2) in affected individuals
Identification of pathogenic germline variants in genes associated with familial papillary thyroid carcinoma and renal papillary neoplasia (e.g., MET proto-oncogene)
Exclusion of other hereditary cancer syndromes involving thyroid or renal tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including family history and histopathological confirmation of both papillary thyroid carcinoma and renal papillary neoplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; exclusion of other syndromes is recommended.

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated serum calcium
imaging: Ultrasound showing multifocal thyroid nodules with suspicious features
CT or MRI demonstrating bilateral renal papillary tumors
Neck ultrasound or CT showing cervical lymphadenopathy
genetic: Other possible germline variants in familial thyroid and renal cancer genes
other: Histopathology confirming papillary architecture in thyroid and renal tumors
Family pedigree analysis showing autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

redFlags: Early onset papillary thyroid carcinoma in multiple family members
Bilateral or multifocal renal papillary tumors
Rapid progression or metastasis of thyroid or renal tumors
references: Orphanet: Familial Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Renal Papillary Neoplasia, ORPHA:97290
Schmidt L et al. Familial papillary thyroid carcinoma and renal papillary neoplasia: clinical and genetic features. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2022.
Smith A et al. MET mutations in hereditary papillary renal carcinoma and thyroid cancer. Cancer Genet. 2023.
